mathematical_checks.assessment: Row1.1 supplies finite diagonalization by a nonzero value and orthogonal splitting, including the zero form. Maximal definite-subspace dimensions prove congruence invariance and block additivity; all selections occur in a fixed finite dimension. The2x2 trace/determinant tests are justified by the explicit real eigenvalue formula, without any infinite-dimensional spectral theorem.

For w=a-b, A andB are integral symmetric, and B has quadratic form|x+wy|^2+b|y|^2, detB=b>0. The4x4 skew part is the standard symplectic block with determinant1. Negation retains determinant1 in even4dimension; the8x8 direct sum therefore has determinant1.

For h=2-2cos(theta)>0 and c=1-exp(i theta), |c|^2=h. Direct block elimination yields C=hA-B^-1 and positive hB. Independently expanded detC=(1-2wh-bh^2)/b and trC=-trB^-1<0. The unique positive root is(-w+sqrt(w^2+b))/b. Below/at/above it the total signature is0/1/2 exactly; a root outside(0,4) simply gives no crossing on the given theta interval. h=0 is separately the zero matrix.

mathematical_checks.topic: General threshold density and error control
mathematical_checks.assessment: For r in(-1,1), a_b=floor(br) gives d_b=1-a_b/b>0 and s=d_b+sqrt(d_b^2+1/b). The bound |s-2(1-r)|<=2/b+1/sqrt(b) follows from floor error and sqrt(d^2+x)-d<=sqrt(x). In fact these approximations are from above; this does not obstruct density or the proof because separate INTERIOR target subintervals are chosen first. Arbitrarily close target values to0 and4 are included by taking sufficiently large b, with no uniform distance-to-endpoint assumption.

mathematical_checks.topic: Arbitrary prescribed containing arc and strict central support
mathematical_checks.assessment: Any open I containing interior theta0 has two strict subintervals on its two sides. h is strictly increasing, so density supplies one threshold in each himage, both strictly in(0,4). Their crossing angles lie strictly inI and straddletheta0; hence theta0 is not a root and a whole open interval about it has signature2. Ordered block subtraction yields exactly0,1,2,1,0 across the two crossing angles, and zero at the endpoint angles zero and pi. Vanishing offI includes both boundary angles0andpi.

The lower-threshold4block is added and the higher-threshold4block negated, so the middle bump is POSITIVE2. Each crossing has value1 because the singular4block has one zero eigenvalue. Real V gives conjugate Hermitian matrices at opposite angles; complex conjugation preserves real inertia and hence the signature. No comparison with a geometric positive-push knot convention is inferred.

The cited papers motivate dense jumps and bump construction. This proof replaces their generic Alexander-polynomial realization and knot arguments by explicit matrices and inertia; deps[] is coherent for the self-contained finite algebra and elementary real formulas used here. An actual smooth disk-band realization remains a separate genuine obligation.
